brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 anniversary evites (rings, roses, toast, moonlit vows, silver and golden years, tree rings, constellations, lace). Decide how time itself can be shown in motion.
brief.audience: Couples and their adult children planning a celebration; guests across generations, including older eyes.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.
references: Exploration grid: romantic fine-art still lifes, two gold rings on blush silk beside garden roses and glowing candles; soft painterly light; calm silk area for type.

proposals.title: The Measure of a Marriage
proposals.idea: Each evite is a scored page — a single governing proportion derived from the subject's own internal count (tree rings, musical intervals, lunar cycles) — so that time is not illustrated but structurally embedded in the grid itself, and every element hangs from that measure as notes hang from a staff.
proposals.geometry: A vertical golden-section column (1 ∶ 1.618) anchors the live-text block at the lower third; above it, a primary art field divided by the subject's own count — twelve rings yield a twelve-beat grid, a rose's five-petal symmetry yields a pentagonal radial, tree rings are literally traced into concentric band-widths that set column gutters. The grid is fixed in proportion but its unit-count changes per card, making each of the twelve geometrically distinct without being arbitrary. At 390 px the column collapses to a single-axis stack; the proportional ratio is preserved, not abandoned.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (display, italic, tracked at +20 for titles — its ink-trap curves photograph like engraved copper); EB Garamond Regular for venue and date lines, set at a strict 1.5 × the cap-height of the display face to enforce vertical rhythm. All caps used only for single-word anchors (FIFTY YEARS / SILVER / VOWS) at the smallest size, so hierarchy descends by size and weight, never by novelty. No decorative script; the italic axis of Cormorant provides all necessary warmth. Minimum 18 px body on mobile; generous leading at 1.6 em.
proposals.imageLogic: Art plates are photographed from physically constructed still-life tableaux under raking single-source candlelight — a direct citation of Jan van Huysum's lateral-light discipline, not a filter approximation. Each object (lace, rings, rose, goblet) is shot on neutral ground, then the negative space is deliberately overexposed to create a luminous ground that accepts the live-text layer without a mask conflict. The foreground cut-outs (drifting petals, a slowly rotating ring, a constellation point that tracks tilt) are extracted from the same shoot, ensuring material continuity: every floating element shares the same photographic grain and color temperature as the art plate beneath it. No composited stock; no AI-generated plate without a photographed source object to anchor it.
proposals.texture: Raw linen scanned at 1200 dpi forms the base layer — not as a filter but as a WebGL displacement map that gives the foil-shimmer layer topographic variance, so the shimmer follows weave direction rather than moving uniformly. The lace card uses an actual historical lace sample (Bruges-style, Plajah-owned prop) scanned and used as a luminance mask for the bokeh layer, so light leaks only through the lacunae of the pattern. This is textile-as-architecture: the material determines where light is permitted to go.
proposals.motion: Entrance: the art plate fades up over 1.2 seconds — not a dissolve but a calibrated crescendo, like a string section entering pianissimo and reaching mezzo-forte. Then the foreground cut-outs drift in at 0.4 px/frame on a 6-second sinusoidal path (slow enough that older eyes register it as breath, not animation). Tilt-parallax activates on gyroscope input: the ring or rose layer shifts at 60 % of device angle, the background at 30 %, creating depth without vertigo. The foil-shimmer pulses at 4-second intervals triggered by a perlin-noise function seeded to the couple's date — so no two openings are identical, but the pacing is always stately. Candle flicker runs at 12 fps with randomised amplitude ±8 % to match the physiological irregularity of real flame. Reduced-motion mode: parallax and flicker cease; only the entrance fade and a single slow foil pulse at 8 seconds remain — the card i
proposals.productionMethod: Physical still-life sets built and photographed by a Plajah production photographer (or partner studio under brief) for each of the twelve subjects. Linen and lace props sourced and archived as Plajah assets. Photographs processed in Lightroom to a unified color temperature (3200 K, slightly warm) then handed to the Tela build team as layered PSDs. The grid for each card is generated from a parametric script that reads the subject's count (12 rings = 12 units, 50 years = golden ratio applied to 50-beat arc) and outputs the Tela layout JSON — so the geometry is derived, not designed ad hoc. WebGL shaders are written once and parameterised; the linen displacement map and lace luminance mask are swapped per card.
proposals.humanTrace: The candlelight in the art plate is real and unrepeatable — its catch-light on a gold ring cannot be reproduced by a renderer. The linen displacement map carries the physical irregularity of woven thread. The lace luminance mask preserves the hand of the bobbin-lace maker. These are not textures applied over a digital image; they are the structural logic of the light and the surface.
proposals.risk: The discipline of deriving geometry from the subject's count will read as over-engineered to guests who never see the grid. The risk is that the structural intelligence is invisible. That risk is worth taking because invisible structure is what separates an evite that feels right from one that merely looks pretty — the guest cannot name why this card is calmer and more authoritative than a competitor's, but they feel the earned rest of the eye at the text block, and that feeling is the whole brief: intimate, enduring, quietly moving.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want each card's entrance to announce itself — a cascade of petals, a dramatic light-leak flare, a musical swell that tells the viewer they are in the presence of something significant. I will hold that the reveal must not announce itself. The weighted sinusoidal drift and the 1.2-second plate crescendo are the reveal; they are simply not performing. A Jan van Huysum sti

proposals.title: Ink Pressed Into Years
proposals.idea: Each card is built from a physical relief print — carved wood, stamped lino, pressed botanical matter — photographed before any screen touches it, so the invitation carries the literal dent and ink-bleed of time as its primary image.
proposals.geometry: Vertical format, uneven bleed edge on the left margin — the physical print was torn from the registration block rather than trimmed square, so the card reads as a page pulled from something real; type sits in a calm, roughly 40% lower zone where the ink thins to near-white; no grid lines, the structure is the pressure gradient of the print itself
proposals.typography: Freight Display Italic for names and headline — oldstyle figures, open apertures, survives screen compression and aging eyes; Founders Grotesk Text Condensed for date and venue in tracked small caps; both set in live Tela text, never baked; scale jumps hard between the two — display at 48px, detail at 13px — no middle size because middle sizes are polite and this isn't polite
proposals.imageLogic: Twelve physical plates made first: carved woodblock rings, lino-cut roses, monoprint moonlight, stamped lace rubbing, cross-sectioned tree-ring rubbing on tissue, constellation prick-and-rub on black paper — all photographed on a flatbed scanner at 1200dpi with the actual plate still in frame so you see registration marks and ink overflow; the scan IS the art plate in Tela, not a texture overlay on a vector; foreground cut-outs are isolated fragments of the same print — a single petal, a ring arc, a lace hexagon — drifting on tilt as translucent Tela layers
proposals.texture: Ink on dampened Japanese kozo paper, giving visible fibre pull and feathered edges; for silver and golden year cards, a second pass with gold foil pressed by hand into the already-printed block, so the foil only catches the raised ink ridges — exactly the condition where I let digital WebGL foil shimmer earn its place, acting as a varnish over a physical dent, not a decoration on top of nothing
proposals.motion: On load: the scanned plate breathes in — a very slow 4s opacity rise from 0.6 to 1.0, simulating ink drying, not a fade-in; tilt-drift on foreground fragments is slow, max 8px parallax, like petals settling in water; WebGL candle-flicker mask animates only within the inked areas, light leaks bleed through the physical ink channels, not around them; reduced-motion: the plate is static at full opacity, foreground fragments fixed, no flicker — the photograph alone carries enough
proposals.productionMethod: Physical: twelve plates carved or assembled by hand — printmaker makes actual prints, botanist or maker presses actual roses and lace; flatbed scan at high res; Photoshop to isolate foreground elements with intentional rough masking, preserving ink halo; art plate exported as compressed AVIF; Tela document layered: plate → foreground cut-outs → WebGL effects through mask channels keyed to ink density → live text zone; names, dates, venues injected as live Tela variables into the white-to-near-white lower field
proposals.humanTrace: The registration mark from the physical block is left in the top-left corner of every card — a small ink cross, slightly imperfect, that you can see if you look; it is the proof that a human pressed wood to paper before a screen ever loaded
proposals.risk: The scan-as-primary-image approach means the art plate is photographically complex, not vector-smooth — it will feel wrong to clients who expect digital polish, and it compresses less predictably than flat illustration; the torn bleed edge will confuse anyone who expects a card to have a clean frame; worth it because the alternative is another anniversary template that looks like it was never touched, and couples celebrating forty years deserve to feel the weight of a mark someone actually made

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip this to one ring on white and call it honest — but that move removes the evidence, and evidence is the point; a wedding anniversary is not an abstract idea, it is forty years of accumulated pressure, and I am leaving the ink bleed in so you can see it; the Minimalist mistakes erasure for truth

proposals.title: Time Computes the Ring
proposals.idea: Each motif — ring, rose, lace, constellation — is rendered as a live parametric system whose visual state is a direct readout of elapsed years: the geometry literally encodes duration, so the invitation is not decorated with time but constructed from it.
proposals.geometry: A single vertical column, 390px wide, divided by a strict modular grid of 12 equal horizontal bands — one per anniversary year represented in the set. The active card uses its band-count as a structural rule: a 25th-anniversary card occupies 25 micro-increments stacked; the art plate crops to reveal only the bands earned. No decorative border; the edge IS the measurement. Foreground cut-outs sit on a z-axis offset grid: three depth planes at 0 / 24px / 48px parallax travel, never more, so tilt reads as dimensionally coherent rather than theatrical.
proposals.typography: Primary: Freight Display Pro Italic — high-contrast, warm, carries optical weight at 28px on mobile without collapsing. Secondary / data layer: IBM Plex Mono Light at 11px, tracking +80 — the year count, the coordinate, the date rendered as pure parameter output, not decoration. No script faces; the system speaks in two registers: human warmth and machine precision. Names set in Freight Display; all metadata in Plex Mono. Vertical rhythm locked to 8px baseline grid across both families.
proposals.imageLogic: No stock photography. Each art plate is a macro photograph of a physical analogue specimen — actual cross-section of a tree trunk (rings), actual optical diffraction grating producing real spectral light (rings on blush silk replaced by light itself bending through glass), actual dried rose petal pressed under a flatbed scanner at 1200dpi, actual lace laid on a lightbox and photographed through a macro lens. These photographs are then run through a custom GLSL shader that isolates the repeating structural unit — the ring count, the cell pattern, the thread crossing — and redraws it as a procedural field. The human photograph underlies; the system traces its logic. Guests see painterly warmth; the rule underneath is computational.
proposals.texture: The base plate reads as soft and luminous because the source is physical light through physical material. The WebGL foil layer is applied ONLY to the parametric trace lines — the counted rings, the lace grid — so shimmer is structurally earned, not scattered. No global glitter. Bokeh particles are seeded at tree-ring node intersections or rose-petal vein termination points extracted from the scan; they drift outward at 0.4px/frame at 60fps, collapsing to still at reduced-motion. Candle flicker is a signed-distance-field mask applied to the luminosity channel of the art plate: the flame is not a separate asset, it is the plate breathing.
proposals.motion: Sequence is a state machine, not a timeline. State 0 — load: art plate renders from centre outward at the rate of one structural unit per 80ms (rings draw in, lace grid weaves, constellation lines trace). State 1 — idle: foreground cut-outs respond to gyro at 12fps, capped arc ±6deg, depth planes separate. State 2 — interaction: tap any motif element and the parametric count re-runs from 1 to N, the year number in Plex Mono increments in sync — guests watch the years accumulate. State 3 — reduced motion: all transitions collapse to a single 200ms opacity fade; gyro disabled; parametric count shown as static final state. No motion is decorative; every animation is a legible data event.
proposals.productionMethod: Physical specimens sourced and photographed in a controlled lightbox setup (tree cross-sections from a timber supplier, dried roses from a botanical press, optical gratings, vintage lace from a textile archive). Scans processed in GLSL to extract structural primitives. Tela document layers: (1) generated art plate as a static WebP with embedded parametric SVG overlay; (2) transparent PNG cut-outs per motif at three depth planes, positioned via Tela's tilt API; (3) WebGL effects layer — foil shimmer on SVG paths, SDF candle mask on art plate luminosity, particle field seeded from scan data; (4) live Tela text block for names, dates, venues. Each of the 12 card variants shares the same shader; the input variable is the anniversary integer N. Changing N changes the structural count, the particle density, the band crop. One system, twelve outputs.
proposals.humanTrace: The flatbed scan at 1200dpi of a pressed rose petal or sawn tree cross-section is the irreducible human trace — the specific specimen, its particular asymmetry, the slight compression artifact at the scanner edge. The GLSL shader does not erase this; it reads the actual pixel luminance of that specific object to place its parametric nodes. Every card carries the fingerprint of a real material thing that existed in a real room.
proposals.risk: The Plex Mono data-layer and the parametric draw-in risk reading as cold or technical to guests who want pure romance. That risk is worth taking because it is the only direction that makes time itself the medium rather than a metaphor — every other approach illustrates time; this one computes it. The warmth is preserved in the photographic substrate and Freight Display; the precision is the argument.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will load the rose and candlelight motifs with maximum luminosity and reveal-sequence spectacle — a slow bloom, a dramatic wipe, a golden cascade. I expect the argument that my parametric draw-in is too legible as mechanism, that mystery requires withholding the rule. I reject this: the rule IS the intimacy. proposals.title: Field Notebooks of Enduring Places
proposals.idea: Each of the twelve motifs is rendered as a specific, located, hand-documented artifact — a ring is a rubbing from a particular brass door-knocker in Essaouira, a rose is a pressed specimen from a Pugliese garden recorded in 1987, a constellation is a fisherman's navigation chart from Sulawesi — so that time is shown not as abstraction but as the accumulated documentary evidence of real things persisting in real places.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 with a field-notebook bleed margin of 18px on all sides, ruled in faint graphite — not decorative but functional, the kind a person actually measures and draws in. The art plate is divided asymmetrically: roughly 62% image field, 38% annotated margin. The margin carries live text. No centered composition; all anchoring is to the left spine, as a bound notebook opens. Type and image share the same plane rather than layering decoratively over one another.
proposals.typography: Headings: iA Writer Quattro — a monospaced documentary face that reads as field annotation, not romance script. Date and venue: Reforma 1918 Light, a Mexican type family with pre-Columbian proportion influence, used at 13px / 22px leading for the older-eye constraint. No script faces anywhere. Letterpress-impression effect achieved by a WebGL displacement mask derived from actual photographic scans of 1960s Letraset sheets — the mask gates the foil shimmer so luster only appears in the micro-dents of letterforms, not as a wash. All caps suppressed; sentence case throughout. A second script line — Devanagari or Arabic or Latin depending on the couple's declared language — sits at equal weight beneath every heading, never subordinate, never decorative.
proposals.imageLogic: The art plate is a composite documentary photograph: a macro shot of the actual motif object (a real rubbing, a real pressed specimen, a real woven textile fragment) shot under raking daylight on 400 ISO film, then drum-scanned at 1200dpi. The scan is the source file — no AI generation, no stock. Grain is preserved and amplified slightly with a luminosity blend. The foreground cut-out layer holds a single translucent object (a botanical silhouette, a ring shadow) that drifts 4px on tilt — slow, tide-like, not playful. Nothing is composited that was not first photographed as a physical thing.
proposals.texture: The base plate reads as heavyweight cartridge paper — achieved by overlaying a 1:1 photographic scan of Fabriano Artistico 300gsm cold-press surface at Multiply 28% opacity. The foil shimmer WebGL layer is gated entirely by the physical tool-marks in the scanned source object: the chisel-lines in the Essaouira brass rubbing, the vein-topology of the pressed rose. Shimmer only lives inside those topographic valleys and ridges — it cannot bleed into the paper field. Candle-flicker bokeh is suppressed to a single warm catch-light that pulses at 0.3Hz, within reduced-motion budget.
proposals.motion: On load: the cartridge-paper texture fades in over 600ms — the paper appears before the image, as if a notebook is being opened. Then the documentary photograph resolves from grain to clarity over 900ms (a film-developing rhythm, dark to light, not a fade). The foreground silhouette drifts in response to gyroscope tilt, max 4px, eased with a 400ms lag — the feeling of something pressed under glass shifting slightly as you turn a book. The foil shimmer activates only when the screen is tilted past 15 degrees — it is earned by the gesture of looking closely, not ambient. Reduced motion: paper fade only, everything else static. No looping animations. Time is shown as accumulation and stillness, not as movement.
proposals.productionMethod: Twelve source objects are physically acquired or documented with maker permission — the brass rubbing requires a letter to the Essaouira medina cooperative; the pressed rose requires provenance documentation from the Puglia botanical archive; the Sulawesi star chart is used only if a collaboration agreement is signed with the community holding it, and that chart is credited by name inside the evite margin. Each object is photographed or rubbed or scanned in the Plajah studio. Drum scans are prepared in 16-bit TIFF. The Tela document layers: (1) Fabriano paper scan plate, (2) documentary photograph plate, (3) WebGL foil-and-flicker layer masked by the tool-mark topology extracted as a greyscale height map from the source scan, (4) foreground cut-out drifting on gyroscope, (5) live text in the margin. Names, dates, venues are Tela text fields — never baked. QR link preview crops to the upp
proposals.humanTrace: The drum-scan grain of the source object is the primary human trace — every registration error in the Essaouira rubbing, every pressed-petal vein in the rose specimen, every hand-ruled line in the navigation chart is present at 1:1 in the final file. The foil shimmer is topographically gated by those marks. A viewer who looks closely enough will see that the light follows the pressure of a specific hand in a specific place on a specific day. The maker's name and location appear in the margin annotation at 10px — small but present, always.
proposals.risk: This direction risks feeling archival or pedagogical rather than celebratory — a couple opening an anniversary evite may want warmth, not a field report. The counter-argument is that specificity IS warmth: knowing that the rose on your evite grew in a named garden in 1987 is more intimate than knowing it is a pretty pink shape. The deeper risk is the collaboration-gating on the Sulawesi chart and any other living-community motif: if permission is not secured, that motif must be replaced, and the creative team must be prepared to do so without complaint. I would rather substitute a motif than proceed without consent.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will reach for the constellation and the golden-years motifs as occasions for maximalist celestial gold — sweeping astrolabe tracery, gilded vellum, operatic scale. I expect a direction that treats the Sulawesi navigation chart as visual material without asking who drew it or whether they are owed a conversation. The Dramatist's grandeur is real and I respect it, but borrowed

proposals.title: The Curtain Rises on Time
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature baroque stage — a single, breathtaking reveal where time is made visible as physical depth: layers of translucent scrim, raking candlelight, and a foreground object that drifts in tilt-parallax like a prop being carried toward you from the wings.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 stage-flat proportions subdivided into three depth planes: a deep-focus painted ground (full bleed, slightly vignette-burned at edges), a middle scrim layer carrying the motif (rings, roses, lace etc.) as a sculptural silhouette, and a raked foreground plane — narrow, angled 8° off horizontal — that holds the live type as if chalked onto the apron of a stage. The scrim layer is offset 18px down from dead-centre so the eye reads it as hanging, not floating. No grid lines visible; structure is all implied by depth and light fall.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond Italic, tracked at -10 to pull letterforms close like whispered words, set at 52–60px for names, 28px for dates. Secondary labels: Cormorant SC (small caps), 14px, 200 tracking, for venue and time — read as an engraved caption. No sans-serif anywhere. Hierarchy is achieved entirely by size and weight contrast within the same family so that at 390px the page feels unified rather than busy. Minimum body size 16px for reduced-vision guests.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Each plate is a painted art composition referencing the Dutch and Flemish still-life tradition — specifically Ambrosius Bosschaert's flowers and Jan Davidsz. de Heem's candlelit banquet pieces — reinterpreted in a contemporary oil-over-digital technique: physical brush marks on linen are photographed, colour-corrected, then composited under a generated lighting pass so every plate has a single identifiable raking light source entering from the upper left. The motif objects (roses, rings, lace, tree cross-sections) are rendered as layered Tela cut-outs with visible edge imprecision — they look cut from a physical oil study, not masked in Photoshop.
proposals.texture: Ground layer: photographed raw linen canvas scanned at 600dpi, desaturated and multiplied beneath the painted composition at 35% opacity — gives the whole image the grain of a stretched canvas. Scrim layer: a thin noise texture (2px grain) applied over the motif cut-outs at 20% so they read as slightly fabric-like. The WebGL foil-shimmer mask runs only over the gold and silver motif elements (rings, candle flame edges, lace threading), activated by tilt — at rest it is dormant; tilted 15°+ it catches the light as real metal leaf would. Candle flicker is a looped 8-frame-per-second particle layer, deliberately stepping rather than interpolating, referencing the wooden toy observation — the mechanical hesitation makes the flame feel more present, not less.
proposals.motion: Sequence: (1) The ground painting fades in over 600ms — a slow reveal as if a curtain is being raised, not cross-dissolved. (2) At 700ms the middle-plane motif drops 6px and locks — one single weighted settle, like a prop being placed. (3) At 1100ms the foreground text plane slides up 4px from below frame — the apron rising to meet the eye. (4) Tilt-parallax is live from that point: ground moves at 0.3× gyro, scrim at 0.7×, foreground at 1.0× — depth is felt, not announced. (5) The foil shimmer on gold/silver activates on tilt over 12°. (6) Candle flicker and bokeh particles breathe continuously at 8fps stepped. Reduced-motion: all positional animation is removed; foil shimmer fires once on load at 40% opacity then holds still; candle flicker becomes a static glow mask. Total load budget: art plate serves as a single optimised WebP at 120kb; cut-outs are SVG paths with painted fill bitma
proposals.productionMethod: Each of the 12 motifs is first built as a small physical tabletop still-life under a single tungsten lamp — actual roses, borrowed rings, real lace pinned to foam board — and photographed as a lighting reference only. That reference photograph is never used in the final art; it is the brief given to the digital painter. The painted plate is rendered in Procreate on an iPad Pro using a custom linen-grain brush, exported as a layered PSD, then the motif elements are separated into Tela cut-out layers. The linen canvas texture is a studio scan. The WebGL shader for foil shimmer is a thin custom GLSL fragment (under 4kb) that reads device orientation via the Gyroscope API. All 12 share the same Tela template structure; only the art plate, cut-out motifs, and colour temperature of the WebGL light-leak change per design.
proposals.humanTrace: The physical still-life photograph used as a lighting reference is embedded invisibly in the Tela document metadata and is accessible to any designer who opens the file — it is the proof that a human hand arranged a real rose and a real candle in a real room before a single pixel was painted. The brush marks on the linen in the painted plate are not smoothed; they remain directional, catching the imported canvas grain so that the stroke of the painter's wrist is legible at 200% zoom.
proposals.risk: The stepped 8fps candle flicker and the single weighted settle of the motif layer will read to some product reviewers as a bug or an unfinished animation. That risk is worth carrying because the mechanical hesitation is the entire emotional argument — it is what separates a living stage from a screensaver. The Radical Minimalist will say the depth layers and foil shimmer are decorative excess. I say: excess applied with precision is not excess, it is scale matched to emotion, and a 40th anniversary deserves a stage that knows it is a stage.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will propose that time be shown through a single element — perhaps a fading opacity or a lone typographic counter — and call it restraint. I call it a decision deferred. 'Intimate' does not mean 'thin.' The couples opening this evite have lived decades together; the design owes them depth they can feel when they tilt their phone and the roses shift against the candlelight. Restraint

proposals.title: One Interval, Precisely Held
proposals.idea: Time is shown not as ornament but as measurement: a single hairline rule advances one pixel per year, and everything else is removed until that motion is the only thing left to feel.
proposals.geometry: 390px fixed column. Full-bleed vertical rectangle divided by a single horizontal hairline at the golden ratio (61% from top). Above: image field. Below: type field. No margin decoration. No corner treatment. The hairline is the design. Grid is 1px stroke on a field of near-white (#F7F5F2) — warm enough to read as paper, cold enough to read as intention.
proposals.typography: Canela Text (Commercial Type) for names and the year figure — optical-size roman, tracked at -10, set large enough that the numeral alone fills approximately 40% of the type field width. Suisse Int'l Mono (Swiss Typefaces) for date, venue, and all logistical copy — 11px, uppercase, tracking +120. No italic. No script. The contrast between the serifed numeral and the monospace detail IS the typographic event. Reduced-motion fallback: all type static at final position.
proposals.imageLogic: A single macro photograph: one material object per card, lit by a single directional source, shot on a flatbed or lightbox so shadow is architectural and not atmospheric. Rings: two gold bands on unbleached linen, shot from directly above — the negative space between them is the subject. Roses: one petal, backlit, cell structure visible — the rose is not romantic, it is biological and therefore permanent. Tree rings: a cross-section slice at actual scale, the rings counted and the anniversary year's ring marked with a single red thread. Moonlit vows: one window rectangle of projected light on a bare plaster wall — no moon visible, only its evidence. Each image is desaturated 40%, then a single warm tone (raw umber wash) is added in the generated art plate. The image never bleeds — it sits inside the golden-ratio rectangle above the hairline, with a 16px inset on all four sides, like a sp
proposals.texture: The art plate carries one texture layer: photographic grain from a scanned sheet of Hahnemühle 308gsm cold-press watercolour paper, overlaid at 12% opacity in Multiply. This is the only texture. It is not decorative; it tells the eye this surface was once touched. The WebGL foil layer is constrained to the hairline only — on tilt, the hairline itself catches light and shifts from warm silver to cold gold. Nothing else shimmers. The bokeh and particle layers are masked to zero on this direction.
proposals.motion: Sequence: 1. Image plate fades in over 800ms, ease-in-out. 2. Hairline draws left-to-right at exactly 1200ms — the duration of one slow breath. 3. Names appear above the hairline: opacity 0 to 1, 600ms, no movement. 4. Year numeral counts up from 01 to the actual anniversary number at 80ms per increment, then holds. 5. Venue and date type fades in beneath, 400ms. 6. Tilt parallax: image plate shifts ±6px on device tilt, foreground cut-out (the object itself, isolated) shifts ±14px — depth without drama. Total open-to-legible: under 3 seconds. Reduced-motion: steps 1 and 3 and 5 only, no counting, no draw, no parallax.
proposals.productionMethod: Art plate: macro photography on controlled flatbed, post-processed in Lightroom (desaturate, tone wash), exported as WebP at 390×475px, under 120kb. Grain overlay: scanned paper texture baked into the plate at export. Hairline and year counter: SVG path animation + vanilla JS counter, no library dependency. Tilt parallax: DeviceOrientation API with graceful fallback to cursor position on desktop. WebGL foil: single-pass shader on the hairline SVG element only — smallest possible GPU footprint. Foreground cut-outs: PNG with transparency, hand-masked in Photoshop. Tela live text layer sits above all. Total estimated load: under 400kb on 3G.
proposals.humanTrace: The flatbed photograph. Every object is placed by hand on the lightbox glass and photographed at actual scale. The shadow cast by the ring, the cell wall of the rose petal, the red thread through the tree-ring slice — these are not generated and not composited. The grain of the paper scan carries the physical history of a sheet that was once wet and dried under tension. These marks are not styled; they are residue.
proposals.risk: This direction risks feeling cold or clinical to couples who came for warmth. The bet is that the coldness is structural and the warmth is material — that the hairline advancing is more emotionally precise than a hundred rose petals falling, because it asks the viewer to feel duration rather than receive sentiment. If the photography is not absolutely exact — if the flatbed light is uneven, if the linen is wrong, if the ring is not perfectly centred — the whole direction collapses into sterility. The risk is worth it because every other direction in this brief will give couples what they expect. This gives them what they will remember.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that a single hairline cannot carry twelve different emotional registers — that rings require fullness, that candlelight requires flicker, that lace requires density. I say: lace is already a grid. The Dramatist is adding until something happens. I am removing until only the thing that matters can. The year counter advancing IS the candle flickering. disputes.objection: The depth-plane sequence — ground, scrim, foreground — is a convincing spatial grammar, but the reveal announces itself so loudly that the content becomes a pretext for the mechanism; when the curtain is the subject, the marriage it commemorates is demoted to occasion. Cormorant Garamond Italic at negative tracking, no sans counterpoint, all within one family: the typographic hierarchy is achieved by size alone, which is not hierarchy but graduated loudness, and at 390px the weight contrast between 60px and 28px within the same cut collapses faster than the proposal admits. The Bosschaert reference is specific and I respect its precision, but compositing brush-on-linen over a generated light
disputes.concession: The decision to step the candle flicker at 8fps rather than interpolate it is structurally correct — mechanical hesitation enforces the rhythm rather than dissolving it, and that is precisely the kind of governed motion I have been reconsidering in my own notes.

disputes.objection: The painted plate is the tell — 'oil-over-digital technique' with brush marks photographed and then composited under a generated lighting pass is exactly the laundering operation I distrust most: a human gesture is used as alibi for a process that could have been undone and redone a thousand times before anyone called it done. The Flemish citations are name-dropped, not earned — Bosschaert arranged real decaying flowers under real mortality; this stages a fiction of that risk without taking it. And the scrim layer, the curtain metaphor, the 'prop being placed' — all of it is theater about theater, which is the most protected position available.
disputes.concession: The 8fps stepped candle flicker — refusing to interpolate, letting the frame stutter — that is a genuine material decision, and it is more honest than anything smooth would be.

disputes.objection: The three-plane stage is a spatial metaphor without a spatial rule — the parallax ratios (0.3×, 0.7×, 1.0×) are chosen for dramatic feel, not derived from any property of the subject, so the depth is decorative assertion rather than a system that changes when the input changes. The 8fps stepped candle flicker is cited as referencing a mechanical observation, which I respect, but it is deployed as atmosphere, not as a parameter tied to anything — it would run identically on a ten-year card and a fifty-year card, which means the motion is a screensaver, not a behaviour. Cormorant at -10 tracking for whispered intimacy is a literary metaphor doing the work that a structural rule should be doing
disputes.concession: The decision to leave the physical brush-stroke direction legible at 200% zoom — and to embed the source photograph in file metadata as a verifiable human trace — is exactly the kind of accountability I want to see in every direction, and it is more rigorous than most teams bother with.

disputes.objection: The red thread through the tree-ring slice is the most specific, attributable, human thing in any of these five proposals — and then the direction immediately dissolves its own logic by calling the desaturated-plus-raw-umber-wash treatment universal, as if warm tone belongs to no tradition and no hand. 'One Interval, Precisely Held' names precision as its ethic but the image logic is a mood, not a provenance: a petal backlit on a lightbox could be Hiroshi Sugimoto's studio, a Polish botanical archive, a Ghanaian herbarium, or a secondary-school science lab, and this proposal refuses to say which, because naming would crack the minimalism. The Minimalist's standing argument is that there is n
disputes.concession: The hairline that catches WebGL foil shimmer only on tilt, and only on the hairline itself, is the most disciplined application of digital luster in any of the five proposals — shimmer structurally earned by restraint, which is exactly the constraint I argued for in my own recent notes.

disputes.objection: The hairline advancing one pixel per year is a beautiful sentence about a design, but a design it is not — it transfers the entire emotional weight of a marriage milestone onto a single 1px stroke and calls that a decision when it is actually a deferral; the macro photograph of two rings on linen shot from directly above is compositionally neutral by deliberate choice, which means the image has been deliberately emptied of the very thing the occasion demands: the feeling of accumulated time pressing on a body. A reveal that arrives at legibility in under three seconds and then holds perfectly still has not honored the event — it has processed it. The scale does not match the emotion, and no
disputes.concession: The red thread marking the anniversary year's ring on the cross-section slice is exactly right — specific, handmade, unrepeatable, and genuinely moving in the way only a small precise gesture can be.

disputes.objection: The three-plane stage geometry is not structure — it is scenery pretending to be structure; depth created by vignette, scrim-offset, and a tilted text apron is theatrical dressing, not a load-bearing spatial logic, and the result is a frame full of decisions that all say the same thing: more. Cormorant tracked tight at every scale, painted linen, stepped candle flicker, bokeh, foil on tilt — each element is individually defensible but together they form a room where every surface is speaking at once and the silence has been entirely consumed. The 8° apron angle is the tell: it exists to feel dramatic, not because the angle carries any meaning the work could not survive without.
disputes.concession: The single identifiable raking light source entering from upper left is a genuine structural discipline — one light origin forces every element into a coherent spatial relationship, and that is exactly the kind of invisible constraint that earns its place.

synthesis.direction: Each of the twelve evites is governed by a proportion derived from its own subject's internal count — twelve rings yield a twelve-beat vertical grid, five rose petals a pentagonal radial, tree rings traced into the column gutters — so the geometry is not designed but derived, and the guest feels its authority without being able to name it. Art plates are photographed from physically constructed still-life tableaux under a single raking tungsten source (3200 K), with deliberate overexposure of negative space to create a luminous ground that accepts live Tela text without a mask conflict; foreground cut-outs are extracted from the same shoot, sharing grain and color temperature throughout. Type is Cormorant Garamond Italic for display (tracked +20, minimum 18 px on mobile, 1.6 em leading) and EB Garamond Regular for logistical lines — hierarchy by size and weight only, no decorative script, no novelty. Motion is a 1.2-second plate crescendo, a 6-second sinusoidal foreground drift slow enough to read as breath, tilt-parallax at 60/30 percent depth split, and WebGL foil shimmer on a Perlin-noise pulse seeded to the couple's date; reduced-motion retains only the entrance fade and one sl
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The hairline-as-foil-anchor discipline: WebGL shimmer is constrained to one structural element per card — the governing proportion line — so it is earned by restraint, not scattered as ambient decoration. This replaces the Classical direction's more diffuse shimmer and makes the structural logic briefly, beautifully visible on tilt.
synthesis.editorCut: The Futurist removed the Plex Mono data-layer and the parametric draw-in counter. Both read as cold mechanism in a brief whose emotional register is intimate and enduring; the year count advancing in monospace belongs to a dashboard, not a marriage. The physical-specimen sourcing and GLSL structural tracing are retained as a production discipline — the Futurist's rigor applied to the Classical's warmth — but nothing in the final card signals its own computation to the guest.
synthesis.openDecision: Photography versus painting: the Classical direction calls for physically constructed still-life photographs as the art plate source; the Baroque direction proposes painted compositions (Procreate on linen grain, referencing Bosschaert and de Heem) with the photograph used only as a lighting reference. The council did not resolve this. Photographs carry unrepeatable candlelight catch and material
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team gave me six distinct philosophies and I am not averaging them. I am taking the Classical direction as lead — geometry derived from each subject's own internal count, photographed still-life plates under a single raking light, type in one family governed by proportion, motion that breathes rather than performs — because it is the only approach that makes the design feel inevitable rather than chosen, and 'inevitable' is what enduring means.

The sharpest disagreement on the council was between the Classical Mind and the Baroque Dramatist. The Dramatist argued that depth, flicker, and reveal sequence are not excess but scale matched to emotion — that couples who have lived decades together deserve a stage that knows it is a stage. I took the Classical side: when the curtain is the subject, the marriage it commemorates is demoted to occasion. The Dramatist's 8-fps stepped candle flicker and single raking light origin are structurally honest decisions I have kept; the three-plane theatrical reveal is not.

The Radical Minimalist made the strongest single edit in the entire session. The hairline catching foil shimmer only on the one structural element, only on tilt, is the most disciplined application of digital luster any director proposed. I have borrowed it exactly: in the final system, WebGL shimmer lives only on the governing proportion line of each card — visible briefly as the guest tilts their phone, then gone. Everything else the Minimalist stripped was stripped too far; a hairline cannot carry twelve different emotional registers, and the Futurist was right to say so.

One decision remains yours, and it is the one the council genuinely could not close: whether the art plates are photographs or paintings. I have a preference — photographs, because the catch-light on a gold ring under real candlelight cannot be reproduced — but two motifs in the set (moonlit vows, constellations) may resist the camera, and you should decide whether to solve that with a hybrid or hold the photographic discipline all the way through.

The coldness is structural and the warmth is material — the hairline advancing is more emotionally precise than a hundred rose petals falling, because it asks the viewer to feel duration rather than receive sentiment.
